JEE Adv 2016 Paper 1 Q20: Irreversible expansion against constant $P_{ext}=3.0$ atm: $w = -P\Delta V = -3.0$ L atm $= -303.9$ J. Isothermal ideal gas, so $\Delta U = 0$ and $q_{sys} = +303.9$ J, which the surroundings lose. $\Delta S_{surr} = -q_{sys}/T = -303.9/300 = -1.013$ J K$^{-1}$. Trap: $nR\ln 2 = 5.763$ is $\Delta S$ of the system, not the surroundings.
JEE Adv 2016 Paper 1 Q21: Atomic radii increase down Group 13, except that Ga is smaller than Al: the poorly shielding 3d electrons raise $Z_{eff}$ (d-block contraction). Order: Ga < Al < In < Tl.
JEE Adv 2016 Paper 1 Q22: Paramagnetic: $[\mathrm{NiCl_4}]^{2-}$ (tetrahedral $d^8$, 2 unpaired), $\mathrm{Na_3[CoF_6]}$ (high-spin $d^6$, 4 unpaired), $\mathrm{CsO_2}$ (superoxide $\mathrm{O_2^-}$, 1 unpaired). Diamagnetic: $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$, low-spin $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2}]^+$, peroxide $\mathrm{Na_2O_2}$. Total = 3.
JEE Adv 2016 Paper 1 Q23: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene. Hydrogenating the C=C in each $-\mathrm{CH_2C(CH_3)=CHCH_2}-$ unit gives $-\mathrm{CH_2CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_2}-$, i.e. alternating ethylene and propylene units: an ethylene-propylene copolymer.
JEE Adv 2016 Paper 1 Q37: Roots of $x^2-2x\sec\theta+1=0$ are $\sec\theta\pm\tan\theta$; since $\tan\theta<0$, the larger is $\alpha_1=\sec\theta-\tan\theta$. Roots of $x^2+2x\tan\theta-1=0$ are $-\tan\theta\pm\sec\theta$, so $\beta_2=-\tan\theta-\sec\theta$. Hence $\alpha_1+\beta_2=-2\tan\theta$.
JEE Adv 2016 Paper 1 Q38: No boy: $\binom64\cdot4=60$. One boy: $\binom41\binom63\cdot4=320$ (the factor 4 picks the captain). Total $=380$. Trap: forgetting the captain gives 95.
JEE Adv 2016 Paper 1 Q39: Multiply by $\sin x\cos x$: $\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x = 2(\cos^2x-\sin^2x)$, i.e. $\cos(x-\pi/3)=\cos 2x$. So $2x=\pm(x-\pi/3)+2k\pi$, giving $x=-\pi/3+2k\pi$ or $x=\pi/9+2k\pi/3$. In $S$: $-\pi/3, \pi/9, 7\pi/9, -5\pi/9$, whose sum is $0$.
JEE Adv 2016 Paper 1 Q41: Need $4\alpha \ge \max_{x>0} \frac{x-1}{x^3}$. The derivative of $(x-1)/x^3$ is $(3-2x)/x^4$, so the maximum is at $x=3/2$: $\frac{1/2}{27/8}=\frac{4}{27}$. Hence $\alpha\ge \frac1{27}$.
